Case Name: Rivera v. National Steel and Shipbuilding Company et al.
Case No.: 24CV443480
This matter comes on for hearing before the Honorable Theodore C. Zayner on March
25, 2026, at 1:30 p.m. in Department 19. The Court now issues its tentative ruling as follows:
I. Introduction
This is a representative action arising from alleged wage and hour violations. Plaintiff
Jorge Rivera (“Plaintiff”) began this action by filing a Complaint against defendant National
Steel and Shipbuilding Company (“NASSCO”) and other entities, asserting a sole cause of
action for civil penalties pursuant to the Private Attorneys General Act (“PAGA”).5 Plaintiff
then filed a first amended complaint (“FAC”), asserting a sole cause of action for PAGA
violations against NASSCO, removing the additional defendants named in the complaint.
Plaintiff Rivera alleges NASSCO required aggrieved employees to perform off-the-clock work,
denied meal periods and rest breaks, auto-deducted meal period time, and failed to provide
accurate wage statements as required by the Labor Code. (FAC at ¶¶ 9-31.)
In another action, plaintiff Marion J. Carroll filed a complaint against defendants
Ameri-Force Craft Services, Inc. (“Ameri-Force”), and NASSCO in San Diego County
(Carroll v. Ameri-Force Craft Services, San Diego County Superior Court, No.
24CU016935C), asserting a sole cause of action for civil penalties pursuant to PAGA.6 Plaintiff
Carroll filed a petition for coordination to coordinate Carrol, and on October 9, 2025, this
Court issued an order denying the petition for coordination.
5 The other entities are: General Dynamics Land Systems, Inc.; General Dynamics Ordnance
and Tactical Systems, Inc.; General Dynamics Information Technology, Inc.; General Dynamics Mission Systems, Inc.
6 In addition to the PAGA claim asserted in the Carroll Action, Plaintiff Carroll also filed a
separate class action in San Diego County on October 6, 2024: Carroll v. Ameri-Force Crafts
Services, Inc. (San Diego County Superior Court, No. 37-2024-00026601; removed to the
United States District Court for the Southern District of California as Case No. 3:24-cv-1443-
RSH-BJC).

The parties have reached a settlement, and Plaintiff has filed a motion for approval of
the PAGA settlement. The motion is unopposed. At the initial hearing on the motion held on
February 25, 2026, the Court continued the motion and instructed Plaintiff’s counsel to
provide: (1) a copy of the separate individual settlement agreement referenced in the PAGA
settlement agreement; and (2) a copy of Plaintiff’s declaration in support of the requested
service award, also referenced in the PAGA settlement agreement. (See Minute Order,
February 25, 2026, p. 4.)
II. Supplemental Filings
On March 13, 2026, Plaintiff’s counsel filed a Joint Submission in Support of
Plaintiff’s Motion for Approval of PAGA Settlement (“Joint Submission”), in which counsel
asserts:
[T]he Parties also hereby inform the Court that there is and will be no separate
individual agreement between Plaintiff and NASSCO. The Parties’ intent was
that the only monetary consideration to Plaintiff himself other than his
settlement sum would be the enhancement payment, and no further formal
agreement is needed because Plaintiff is a former employee who has agreed to a
general release as a pre-condition to the enhancement payment (as disclosed in
the settlement agreement already on file with the Court).
(Joint Submission, p. 3:17-22.)
Also on March 13, 2026, Plaintiff’s counsel submitted the declaration of Victoria Mas
addressing the Court’s request for a copy of Plaintiff’s declaration in support of the requested
service award. Ms. Mas explains that she has recently assumed responsibility for this matter
and is actively attempting to locate Plaintiff Jorge Rivera. (Declaration of Victoria Mas, ¶ 3.)
5. Despite diligent efforts, counsel has experienced delays due to difficulty in
contacting Plaintiff Rivera. Plaintiff’s counsel continues to make good-faith
efforts to establish contact so the declaration may be completed.
6. Accordingly, upon contacting our client, I will promptly ensure that this
declaration is submitted to the Court to avoid any further delay in these
proceedings.
(Mas Decl., ¶¶ 5-6.)
While Plaintiff’s attorneys have submitted additional documents in support of the
motion following the prior hearing on the motion, they have not submitted either of the
requested documents that are referenced in the proposed PAGA settlement agreement.
Counsel’s statements in the supplemental materials appear to be somewhat inconsistent with
the language in the proposed settlement and the initial moving papers, as stated below.
8. This Stipulation of Settlement is made for the purpose of consummating
settlement of the Lawsuit on a representative basis under PAGA with a
corresponding settlement of Plaintiff’s individual claims by way of a
separate Individual Settlement and Release Agreement. … [¶] …
39. This Stipulation of Settlement is the sole and exclusive agreement with
respect to the Released Claims and the resolution of the PAGA claims
asserted in the Lawsuit, and this Stipulation of Settlement supersedes all
prior agreements, written or oral, between or among the Parties regarding
the Released Claims and the resolution of such claims. This Stipulation of
Settlement in no way involves, releases, or settles Plaintiff’s individual
claims, which are subject to a separate settlement and release agreement.
(Declaration of Shaun Setareh [November 6, 2025], Ex. 3 (“Stipulation of Settlement of
Representative Claim Under the California Labor Code Private Attorneys General Act of 2003,
¶¶ 8, 39.)
Plaintiff was first hired by NASSCO in November 2004 as a non-exempt
journeyman shipfitter. He worked for NASSCO during several periods, and his
employment with Defendant was last terminated on May 18, 2023 (Settlement,
¶ 1; Declaration of Jorge Rivera (“Rivera Decl.”), ¶ 2.)
(Motion, p. 3:10-12.)
Awarding Plaintiff just over 0.66% of the GSA is entirely reasonable given
Plaintiff’s efforts in this case undertaken on behalf of absent aggrieved
employees. (Setareh Decl., ¶ 37; Rivera Decl., ¶¶ 6- 11.) In this case, Plaintiff
has devoted over 25 hours of his time advancing the interests of the aggrieved
employees and the State of California. (Id.) Plaintiff has done this by, among
other things, retaining experienced counsel, providing Plaintiff’s Counsel with
extensive information about his work history with Defendant and Defendant’s
policies and practices with respect to the wage and hour claims at issue,
foregoing pursuit of his individual claims in favor of a fair resolution,
participating in a full-day mediation session, and being actively involved in the
settlement process to ensure a fair result for the aggrieved employees and the
State of California as a whole. (Id.)
(Id. at p. 22:16-27.)
Plaintiff faced the risk that he could face worsened career prospects for suing a
former employer for wage and hour violations and serving as the named
plaintiff in a representative action lawsuit. (Setareh Decl., ¶ 37; Rivera Decl., ¶
11.)
(Id. at p. 26:4-6.)
Thus, while Plaintiff’s counsel has submitted supplemental materials following the
initial hearing on the motion, they have not submitted the materials that the Court requested.
Furthermore, counsel’s supplemental materials indicate that the proposed settlement and
moving papers may contain some inaccurate or inconsistent information. Counsel’s inability to
locate Plaintiff also raises the question of whether any service award would in fact be received
by Plaintiff. Because of these inconsistences relating to the motion as currently presented, the
Court cannot approve the proposed PAGA settlement at this time.
III. Conclusion
The motion for approval of PAGA settlement is DENIED without prejudice.
The Case Management Conference set for 2:30 p.m. on March 25, 2026 is
CONTINUED to July 1, 2026 at 2:30 p.m. in Department 19.
Plaintiff shall prepare the order.
